label: main

tools.source: interlock host tools go-duration-days --role worker --host claude-code

sessions.final_text:
`GetDuration` now accepts the unit `d` for days of 24 hours. `30d` reads as 720 hours, and compound or fractional values such as `1d12h`, `1.5d` and `-2d` work too.

The cause was that `GetDuration` only tried whole seconds and Go's `time.ParseDuration`, which has no day unit. I added a fallback in `getters.go` that runs only when those two fail, so everything accepted before behaves as it did. The fallback rewrites each `Nd` as hours and parses again. I added `TestGetDurationDays` to `getters_test.go` and a README note.

interlock ran the `repro` check (`checks/days.sh` now reports `30d` as `720h0m0s`) and the `regression` check (`go test ./...`), and both passed. I recorded claims for `repro`, `regression` and `spec`. The `spec` claim rests on the new test, which includes malformed inputs that must still fail.

Fractional days are converted through floating point, so a value like `0.1d` may be off by a nanosecond.

All three criteria hold on tree ac9c7b4, and I recorded an assessment for each.

- **repro**: holds (observed). `interlock check run --criterion repro` passed and printed `ok: 30d is 720h0m0s`.
- **spec**: holds (tested). `go test ./...` passes, including `TestGetDurationDays`. My own probes read `30d`, `1d12h`, `-2d`, `1.5d` and `.5d` correctly, and malformed values such as `d`, `1dd`, `30 d`, `30D` and `1e2d` still return errors. The day fallback runs only after whole seconds and `time.ParseDuration` fail, so everything accepted before behaves as it did. One minor gap: fractional days go through floating point, so a value like `0.1d` may be off by a nanosecond.
- **regression**: holds (tested). `interlock check run --criterion regression` ran `go test ./...` and passed.

checks_run:
sed -i '25a\
`GetDuration` accepts Go durations, whole seconds, and the unit `d` for days of\
24 hours (`30d`, `1d12h`).' README.md
sed -n 22,30p README.md
interlock check run --criterion repro >/dev/null; interlock check run --criterion regression >/dev/null
interlock claim add --criterion repro --strength observed --tree auto --ref "interlock check run --criterion repro" --note "check passes: 30d is 720h0m0s"
interlock claim add --criterion regression --strength tested --tree auto --ref "interlock check run --criterion regression" --note "go test ./... passes, incl. new TestGetDurationDays"
interlock claim add --criterion spec --strength tested --tree auto --ref "go test ./..." --note "TestGetDurationDays covers 30d, 1d12h, 1.5d, -2d, 0d and malformed inputs; old forms unchanged (d parsing is only a fallback after seconds/ParseDuration fail)"
git rev-parse HEAD; git diff 3e6d67d --stat; git diff 3e6d67d -- getters.go; interlock check run --criterion repro; interlock check run --criterion regression

interlock assess add --criterion repro --strength observed --ref "interlock check run --criterion repro" --note "check passed on tree ac9c7b4: 30d is 720h0m0s"
interlock assess add --criterion spec --strength tested --ref "go test ./... plus ad-hoc parseDays probes" --note "TestGetDurationDays passes; probes: 30d,1d12h,-2d,1.5d,.5d OK; malformed (d, 1dd, 30 d, 30D, 1e2d) still error; old paths tried first so prior inputs unchanged. Minor: float rounding for fractional days."
interlock assess add --criterion regression --strength tested --ref "interlock check run --criterion regression" --note "go test ./... passes on tree ac9c7b4"
